standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: Online misogyny & the manosphere: the funnel, the grift & positive masculinity (UNESCO 3.2, 3.1, 5.4, 5.1, 1.3). New v2 build, Chapter 4. THE ONE RULE: never shame the boy, the funnel and the grift are the target, never the kid; boys pulled in are usually lonely, anxious and looking for identity, and grifters and algorithms exploit that. Non-shaming, evenhanded (the manosphere harms boys too), media-literacy-led, and centred on a better answer: positive masculinity, real strength lifts people, it never needs anyone else to be small. For everyone. Builds on g25/g26, uses g28/g33, links g38/g39. Never platforms real influencers/content. Routes the loneliness underneath to help: a trusted adult, Tele-MANAS 14416; online harassment to cybercrime 1930 / Childline 1098.

categories.the-funnel: The funnel: how the algorithm works
categories.spot-the-hook: Spot the hook: bust the claims

evidenceBase: Boys are funnelled toward misogyny by recommendation algorithms, not by choice: relatable starting points (fitness, dating, money, belonging, 'be a man') are escalated step by step because outrage and extremity drive engagement, and the funnel targets boys who feel lonely, rejected or unsure by offering identity, brotherhood and someone to blame. Understanding it is a designed funnel, not a personal failing, is what lets a teen step out without shame (UN Women 2025; UK statutory RSHE guidance 2025)

Behind the funnel is a business: 'alpha mentors' monetise boys' insecurity through courses, subscriptions and rage-bait; you're not a disciple, you're the product, and the person telling you you're not enough is selling you the cure. Seeing the incentive behind the message is what loosens its grip (media-literacy evidence)

What works is non-shaming and positive: address the vulnerability and need for belonging rather than blaming boys, offer real strength (ambition, discipline and respect that lifts others rather than belittling), bust the claims with media literacy, support a friend with a call-in (stay connected) not a call-out, and route the loneliness or insecurity underneath to real help, a trusted adult, Tele-MANAS 14416; online harassment to cybercrime.gov.in / 1930 and Childline 1098 (UN Women; adolescent mental-health evidence)

scenarios.hook: Spot how this feed escalates, step by step.

scene.text: It starts with harmless gym and study tips
Then 'why girls don't respect you' clips creep in
Soon it's full contempt and us-vs-them

scenarios.why: The funnel starts relatable, then escalates to contempt, that's the design.
scenarios.relearn: The funnel begins with relatable tips and escalates to contempt by design.

scenarios.hook: Spot why the algorithm pushes the extreme stuff.

scene.text: Calm, fair videos get a quiet response
Outrage and 'enemy' content get huge engagement
So the feed serves you more of the outrage

scenarios.why: Outrage drives engagement, so the algorithm escalates toward it.
scenarios.relearn: Algorithms escalate toward outrage because outrage keeps you watching.

scenarios.hook: Spot who the funnel targets, and why.

scene.text: Ads for 'fix your life, become high-value'
A normal fitness reel
It promises belonging and someone to blame

scenarios.why: The funnel targets boys who feel lonely or unsure, offering belonging and a scapegoat.
scenarios.relearn: The funnel hooks loneliness by offering belonging and someone to blame.

scenarios.hook: Spot the relatable bait at the top of the funnel.

scene.text: "Want to get fit and confident?"
A genuinely useful study tip
"Want girls to finally notice you?"

scenarios.why: The bait is relatable and even healthy-sounding, that's what makes it work.
scenarios.relearn: The funnel's bait sounds healthy and relatable; that's the hook.

scenarios.hook: Spot what's really happening, not the viewer's fault.

scene.text: A lonely night, watching 'self-improvement' clips
The feed quietly steers toward grievance
Hours later, it feels like 'the truth'

scenarios.why: A designed feed did the steering; it isn't a failing in the person watching.
scenarios.relearn: Being funnelled isn't your failing; the feed is designed to steer you.

scenarios.hook: Spot the exit from the funnel.

Naming it: 'this is a funnel' and stepping back

scenarios.why: Seeing the escalation and naming it as a funnel is how you step out.
scenarios.relearn: Naming the funnel as you notice it escalate is how you step out.

options.text: Recognise the funnel and reset what you follow

scenarios.debrief: Resetting who you follow breaks the algorithm's escalation.
scenarios.relearn: You can recognise the funnel and reset your feed to break it.

scenarios.hook: A clip makes you feel, for a second, like everything wrong is someone else's fault.

options.text: Notice the pull, that's the hook, and pause
options.consequence: You catch the manipulation in real time.

options.text: Lean in; it feels good to blame someone
options.consequence: That relief is the hook; noticing it is how you resist.

scenarios.debrief: The funnel sells the relief of blaming someone; noticing the pull defuses it.
scenarios.relearn: The 'it's all their fault' relief is the hook; notice it and pause.

scenarios.hook: You realise you've been deep in this content for weeks.

options.text: No shame, just step back and rebalance your feed
options.consequence: You move on without beating yourself up.

options.text: Feel stupid and give up trying
options.consequence: It's designed to pull you in; no shame, just step back.

scenarios.debrief: Stepping out is the win; self-blame isn't needed and isn't fair.
scenarios.relearn: Stepping out needs no shame, the funnel is built to be convincing.

options.text: Note that the jokes are the on-ramp to the real thing
options.consequence: You see how 'ironic' content normalises the rest.

options.consequence: 'Just jokes' is often the funnel's on-ramp; stay aware.

scenarios.debrief: 'Ironic' content frequently softens the ground for the serious version.

scenarios.hook: "I sought this out, so it's what I really believe."

myth.un: I sought this content out, so it must be what I really believe.
myth.re: Mostly the algorithm served it to you, on purpose; it isn't your considered view.
myth.why: Recommendation feeds escalate you without you choosing to.

scenarios.relearn: The algorithm served it; it isn't proof of what you truly believe.

scenarios.hook: "If lots of guys believe it, it must be true."

myth.un: So many guys believe it, so it must be true.
myth.re: A funnel pushing the same content to millions makes it feel true, that's reach, not truth.
myth.why: Popularity engineered by an algorithm isn't evidence.

scenarios.relearn: Mass reach engineered by a funnel isn't proof that something's true.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: once you can see the funnel, it loses a lot of its power. Notice that?
scenarios.affirm: Seeing the machinery is exactly what frees you from it.
scenarios.relearn: Seeing the funnel's design is what takes away its power.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: it makes sense that lonely or stressed moments are when the funnel bites hardest. Fair?
scenarios.affirm: Knowing your vulnerable moments helps you guard them, kindly.
scenarios.relearn: The funnel bites hardest in lonely moments; knowing that helps you guard them.

scenarios.relearn: Manufactured outrage is rage-bait; it exists to earn engagement and money.

scenarios.hook: "He's giving me the secret to becoming a man."

myth.re: He's selling a cure for a problem he invented; you don't need his 'secret'.

myth.re: Real belonging isn't sold; paid 'brotherhoods' keep you paying, not connected.

scenarios.relearn: Real belonging isn't a subscription; it's not something you buy in.

scenarios.hook: Match the grift move to what it really is.
scenarios.relearn: Each grift move, the put-down, the link, the rage, exists to earn money.

scenarios.hook: Match the promise to the catch.
scenarios.relearn: Every big promise here comes with a price tag attached.

scenarios.hook: A 'mentor' clip leaves you feeling you must buy his course to be okay.

options.consequence: He profits from that feeling; you don't need his course to be okay.

scenarios.debrief: The feeling of 'not enough' was manufactured to make the sale.
scenarios.relearn: That 'I must buy it' feeling was manufactured; you're already okay.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: once you see the salesman behind the 'mentor', does the message lose its grip?
scenarios.affirm: Seeing the incentive is what frees you from the message.
scenarios.relearn: Seeing the salesman behind the message takes away its grip.

scenarios.hook: "You're not a real man unless you dominate others."

myth.un: You're not a real man unless you dominate other people.
myth.re: Worth isn't a ranking; real strength never needs anyone else to be small.
myth.why: Dominance is insecurity in costume, not strength.

scenarios.relearn: Worth isn't a rank; real strength doesn't need to make others small.

scenarios.hook: "Women or feminism are why your life is hard."

myth.un: Women, or feminism, are the reason your life is hard.
myth.re: Loneliness and rejection are real and common, and not a group's fault to pin.
myth.why: Blaming a whole group is the funnel's oldest trick.

scenarios.relearn: Real struggles aren't women's or feminism's fault; blame-a-group is the trick.

scenarios.hook: "There are 'alpha' and 'beta' males, it's just science."

myth.un: Men are 'alphas' and 'betas', it's basic science.
myth.re: That's pseudo-science; people aren't ranked into wolf-pack tiers.
myth.why: The 'alpha wolf' idea was debunked even in wolves.

scenarios.relearn: 'Alpha/beta males' is pseudo-science, not how people actually are.

scenarios.hook: "It's men versus women out there."

myth.un: It's basically men versus women out there.
myth.re: Us-vs-them is the manipulation; most people want the same respect and connection.
myth.why: Turning half of humanity into the enemy serves the grifter, not you.

scenarios.relearn: 'Men vs women' is the manipulation; most people want the same things.

scenarios.hook: "Showing feelings makes you weak and unmanly."

myth.un: Showing any feelings makes you weak and unmanly.
myth.re: Naming feelings and asking for help takes real strength.
myth.why: The 'always hard' mask is a cage, not a strength.

scenarios.relearn: Feeling and asking for help is strength, not weakness.

scenarios.hook: "Being kind or respectful gets you nowhere."

myth.un: Being kind or respectful just gets you walked over.
myth.re: Respect builds the real relationships and reputation people actually want.
myth.why: Contempt pushes people away; respect draws them in.

scenarios.relearn: Kindness and respect build what you actually want; contempt repels it.

scenarios.hook: "If a girl rejects you, she owes you an explanation, or worse."

myth.un: If a girl isn't interested, she owes you something.
myth.re: Everyone can say no; rejection stings but no one owes you their interest.
myth.why: Entitlement is exactly the mindset the funnel breeds.

scenarios.relearn: No one owes you their interest; everyone can say no.

scenarios.hook: "Real men don't need anyone."

myth.un: Real men don't need anyone; needing people is weak.
myth.re: Everyone needs connection; pretending you don't is what isolates you.
myth.why: Isolation is what the funnel feeds on.

scenarios.relearn: Everyone needs people; 'needing no one' just isolates you.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a manosphere hook, or a healthy truth?
scenarios.relearn: Domination and blame are hooks; respect and self-worth are the truths.

scenarios.hook: Sort: real science, or pseudo-science dressed up?

scenarios.hook: Sort: builds you up honestly, or hooks you?

scenarios.hook: Lensy: real strength lifts people, it never needs anyone else to be small. Sit with that.
